Educational Insights Raccoon Rumpus Game, Preschool Game with Dice & Color Matching, For 2-4 Players, Fun Family Board Game For Kids Ages 3 to 5 This is a precious little game that I imagine young children will long remember.

You get 4 cards that have a raccoon in his/her underwear. (There are no bras on the underwear cards, just underwear/panties) The basic raccoon cards all look the same, though. The face on the raccoon is a plastic piece that's raised off the card. The outfit cards have a hole where the face goes, so the outfit cards actually fit right onto the raccoon card.

Your little ones will roll two dice. They will get a color and a piece of clothing to look for. For example, if they roll a red and a picture of pants, they will look for a card with a red pair of pants on it. The child that gets 5 outfit cards first, wins.

So, it's a quick game. My 2 year old has a tiny attention span right now, and there's very few games that hold his attention. This game is a good choice for him. It's teaching him his colors, taking turns, types of clothing, counting. It's a wonderful little game!

It's also fun for my 5 year old, but he is delayed. I imagine the perfect average ages for this game is 2-4 years old. It's pretty simple for an older child.

Overall, this is a very cute game, and I highly recommend it for little ones just learning to play games!
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Raccoon Rumpus Game, Preschool Game with Dice & Color Matching, For 2-4 Players, Fun Family Board Game For Kids Ages 3 to 5

text_fidelity_a:
City Fire Station Building Blocks Set W/ Fire Truck, Fire Rescue Helicopter, Drone & Fire Engine Toys, Fire Command Center Playset, Firefighters Roleplay Toy Gifts for Kids Boys Girls Ages 6+ (744PCS) It's fake LEGO. It may pretend it isn't, but it is,
As well as being fake LEGO it has one other claim to fame.
It is very disappointing.
When companies copy (not be inspired by. I am all for being inspired! this is copying) because of patents, they cannot copy the construct of the bricks. So they end up with bricks that do not push together well, giving models less resilience to being knocked over, picked up or even played with.
Except for the tile pieces. They stick like they were coated in gorilla glue! You may need power tools to get them apart.

Aside from the poor quality of the bricks, what else can be said? Nothing good, sadly. The set designs are primitive. The vehicles are not all on the same scale. Some will not hold the minifigs.
The accessories are another disappointment. Ugly, hard for the minifigs to hold.

If you have a nephew or niece who loves LEGO, and you simply cannot stand this family member, you have found the perfect gift.

Otherwise, keep looking. You will pay more for LEGO, and it is worth every cent!
text_fidelity_b: City Fire Station Building Blocks Set W/ Fire Truck, Fire Rescue Helicopter, Drone & Fire Engine Toys, Fire Command Center Playset, Firefighters Roleplay Toy Gifts for Kids Boys Girls Ages 6+ (744PCS)

text_fidelity_a:
Hasbro Gaming Yippie Yippie Yeti Game We just aren't overly fond of this game. It ended up being super frustrating for us.

When you first open the game, you have to put the game board together. This takes a bit of time, but it's not too bad. It looks nice enough, and I like that the game board is thick and sturdy. My boys love the whole idea of the game, and I don't think we've ever played a game where the board stood up. That was really cool! Our biggest issue is how difficult it is to keep the climbers in place. They're constantly falling when they shouldn't be. My children are 3, 5, and 8, so that may have a great deal to do with it. Keeping those climbers hanging where they should proved impossible for us, though. It's also a little frustrating that each player has to move around to play. The game board only faces one way, and you can't move it without making the climbers fall off(even more). That means when 4 people are playing, you can't just sit in a spot and enjoy the game. You have to move around, depending on whose turn it is. That might not be a big deal for many, but it frustrated my little guys.

Overall, we really like the whole idea of the game, and the fact that the game board stands up, but it ended up being incredibly frustrating for everyone.
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Gaming Yippie Yippie Yeti Game

text_fidelity_a:
Hairdorables HairDUDEables Collectible Dolls, Series 1, Styles May Vary, by Just Play CONTEXT
My niece washed a bunch of dishes for me, so in return I purchased a toy for her. She chose this one!

PROS
- The idea is F-ING CUTE AF. Especially for girly girls who love hair and makeup stuff.
- It came with a bunch of different accessories
- This is so affordable!
- It's similar to the very popular LOL dolls in that it's got a bunch of different compartments that you open separately for each accessory
- The box can be used as a display/closet! So cute.

CONS
- It is called "hairdorables" and from reading the box/description I believed my niece would be able to "crimp" the doll's hair with the tools provided. That was NOT the case. Maybe we just did it wrong, or we got a dud tool? Nonetheless, it was very disappointing that it didn't work how we expected it to.

RECOMMENDATION
I do plan on buying this again and would recommend anyone looking for kids who love styling hair and fashion and what not, to get this as well. Just be warned that it may not do what it claims.

I love this puzzle so much that I ended up buying the other two Hogwarts castle ones as well. It only took about 3 hours to complete. I have never done a 3D puzzle and found it rather easy. DO read the instructions while putting up the walls because there is a support piece that goes inside which I missed the first time. Also, there are little pieces that don't appear to go to anything that have little red dash marks on them. I was not sure if I needed them and it turns out you don't. However, I would suggest not throwing them away until after the puzzle is put together. I was missing one piece and found it in with the little pieces because I missed it while sorting the first time!

Smart Tech Sound Action Tunnel Deluxe Set Got this for my toddler - and he loves it! And what little boy wouldn't? It's a very generous set of train toys - so big in fact that it needs to fit in two boxes. The quality of the toys themselves are great - unlike very many toys out there, these feel like they will last for years to come. There's so much variety - but interexchangeability here - that it feels more like legos than anything else - a testament to the creativity of Brio.

The most fascinating thing is that this could be considered a "smart" train set - there is a sensor built into the tunnels so that once the train goes through, it can perform an action like stop, or sound horn. Adds an extra level of interactivity to the set, versus just having it go around in a circle.

The only concern of course is the hefty price tag. It's not cheap, but if you're gearing up for a big birthday bash, this could be the right choice!
text_fidelity_b: Smart Tech Sound Action Tunnel Deluxe Set

Playskool Mr. Potato Head I just wanted to give it 5 stars and be done with the review, but they require a description on Amazon...so I'll post my mom's secret chocolate chip cookie recipe here instead (not so secret anymore, is it, Mom!?):

4 cubes butter, softened
2 heaping cups dark brown sugar (packed, then heap that shiz)
½ cups white sugar
2 tablespoons vanilla
1 ½ teaspoon salt
1 ½ teaspoons baking soda
3 eggs
6 cups flour
1 bag chocolate chips (semi-sweet or sweet)

Mix BY HAND all ingredients, except flour and chips (mixing by hand makes them taste better, trust me).
Then add flour and chips and stir BY HAND. Bake @ 350 for 9-11 minutes on ungreased cookie sheet. Enjoy the preciouses.
Note: makes a buttload of cookies, so you might want to halve the recipe.

Minsk Remote Control Stunt Car Toy, 4WD RC Cars Double Sided Rotating Vehicles 360° Flips to Bloom, 2.4GHz High Speed Rechargeable Toy Presents for 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 Year Old Boy Birthday The car itself is pretty cool. I like the way it moves its entire axels to do its stunts. You can get a pretty good idea of hwo this moves if you look at the pictures. Simple, but effective. Seems like kids younger than 8 would like this; odd because they show small kids crawling on the floor using this, but say it is for ages 8 and up. Just watch they don't try to eat the batteries, I guess. It's not super fast, either, so older kids might get bored.

Anyway, they totally cheaped out on the battery setup. 400mAh?!?! Are you kidding me? Even the cheap, "included" versions of decent brands are 1100mAh, with good ones getting 2500mAh or more. And why the goofy charging setup? You have to take it out and then hook it to an oddball USB cable (so now you can't just use any USB cable you have laying around, you have to have this one on hand). They should just wire a higher capacity battery inside and add a micro-USB port like everybody else. And maybe similar functionality for the controller, which, oddly, uses two batteries...more than the car itself.

Pretty fun. Not well thought out overall, but on the other hand, if your kids falls out of love with toys quickly, maybe it's better not to spend more for the battery setup that could have been...
text_fidelity_b: Minsk Remote Control Stunt Car Toy, 4WD RC Cars Double Sided Rotating Vehicles 360° Flips to Bloom, 2.4GHz High Speed Rechargeable Toy Presents for 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 Year Old Boy Birthday

QMAN Girls Building Blocks Toys Trendy Cosmetics Store Building Kit Girls Make-Up Shop Street-View Bricks Toy for Girls Age 6-12 and Up (348 Pieces) I tried three of these off-brand LEGO sets in the "street store" model series - the coffee house, the make-up store, and the hair salon. Each of the finished stores is too small for your minifigs to actually use, which is quite disappointing - this is a look-at model only - but also like those models, the final product is quite a winner. Smooth bricks cover every surface, so it doesn't even look like a LEGO set when finished.

The instructions are fine, but certainly not as clear as they would be if made by LEGO, who have a long history of writing the best manuals in the business. These will do, but are certainly not entirely clear.

The tilted coffee cup on the roof of the cafe really makes this one stand out, and it offers a lot of interesting pieces that make this one stand out. This is the clear winner of the three I tried, and if I only bought one, this would be it.

The make-up store and the hair salon were both good, but looked a lot more typical when finished. They are quite colorful, and have some unique aspects in the interior. These sets were fine, but slightly more difficult to build, and a little bit more finicky in terms of detail work. The final product is a lot less identifiable, but they still look good on the shelf, and have plenty in them that you can use in other models.
text_fidelity_b: QMAN Girls Building Blocks Toys Trendy Cosmetics Store Building Kit Girls Make-Up Shop Street-View Bricks Toy for Girls Age 6-12 and Up (348 Pieces)

text_fidelity_a: JOON Big Teddy Bear, 30 Inches, Tan Before I give my review of this teddy bear, I will give teddy bear shoppers some information to inform their purchase.  Of the several teddy bears I've bought on Amazon, they tend to be kind of smaller than they are supposed to be in my mind..  Another thing is that they compact the teddy bears in a box and need fluffing out and shaping the form.  This bear is nice, cuddly, and so soft, but after delivering it from the boxed constraints it doesn't seem to have sufficient stuffing for the size and cost.  When someone hugs a teddy bear, they usually want to feel the  bear's fullness and being fully stuffed to  make it feel better for cuddling and comfort.  On a 1 to 10, I'd give it a 8.6 or so.  It is wonderfully soft and cozy but it really could have used more stuffing to fill it out in the apendages (i.e. arms and legs).  It is a fairly good size and is soft!  Ah, yes!  He will come out of the box a little deformed so to speak, but with some care he/she will fill out somewhat better.  Of the bears I've bought on Amazon, I am most happy with this model.  If the manufacturer would use a slightly bigger box and fill the body up more than they do it would be great!  The nose on the teddy bear is rather stiff and not soft at all which is in a way kind of strange!  All in all I am pretty happy with my purchase.  Don't forget to name it and make it yours friend!

Replogle Aragon 12" Desktop World Globe, Raised Relief, Up-to-Date Cartography, Made in USA (Blue Ocean) The review always asks: What did you use this product for?
Well, when we watch the network news at night, I never know, exactly, where the places are that are in the news.
When I'm introduced to a new person who has an accent I just can't place, and when I ask them where they're from and they answer with the the name of a country, that I'm not familiar with, let alone the continent it resides on, I feel like an ass.
And admit it, when you play Jeopardy (and 90% of the world plays Jeopardy) your palms start to sweat when the category is Capitals Of The World.
And you go into overdrive when the Final Answer is: What peninsula (peninsula?) is where the historic treaty of peace (what?) was signed in 2001 between the United States and the Republic of Whatever (OMG).
This replogle globe, which is Made in the United States, is not only beautiful but it holds lots of information. The Legend denotes swamps from canals and shipping routes. You just can't believe what you can "read" on a globe. If you want to know where they are and you are in this world, buy a globe. Buy this one.
Can you name at least three countries that survive Ukraine?
I rest my case.

text_fidelity_a:
Boardwalk Arcade Pop-A-Shot This is video pinball as it used to be, before today's highly sophisticated physics simulators: floaty ball mechanics, dumbed down special features, bizarre flipper behavior, etc. Which is what I expected.

But I have to say, I'm impressed at the care they put into it nevertheless. They carefully reproduced the major playfield features and loops, the special modes, the multiballs, the spinning pizza. They made the marquee its whole own separate screen so they could have the interactive elements. They have a clever alternative for the plunger (hold down the button for longer to shoot harder). The flipper buttons on the side can get a little finger-cramping, so they put duplicates on the back of the unit so you can hold the whole unit. And, for better or for worse, they reproduced all of the boys' voices. Ugh. And unless I'm mistaken, unlike most of the Tiny Arcade series, it actually saves your high scores.

It's not all good - the "Start Game"/"Game Over" text is hilariously blocky, like an Atari 2600 game, and it pops up on the playfield. I don't know why they didn't put it on the marquee LCD where it belonged. The ball vibrates weirdly on the habitrails. A couple times, particularly in multiball, I've had the ball just simply fall through the hinge of the flipper. But these aren't huge concerns, and they're easily laughed off.

One warning for sensitive and/or young users: I've always thought the original pinball game's marquee's presentation of April was excessively sexy (she's a hero in her own right, not eye candy, darn it) but in the cut down version it looks like... uh, something else entirely.

All in all, this way exceeded my expectations. And it's actually quite fun! I'm not interested in the other "boardwalk arcade" games so far, but I'd gladly buy more pinball games like this one if they're at a similar level of playability.
text_fidelity_b: Boardwalk Arcade Pop-A-Shot

Forget having a toddler do this on their own, but if you lose about four pieces, then you should be able to easily fit the remaining pieces. But, I'd recommend throwing the box away, and finding your own box.

They have the numbers 1-20, with the corresponding number of things on the piece. For example, piece number 17 has seventeen butterflies.

Pros:
+Really sticks to a fridge or other surface
+Has the numbers 1-20, with a corresponding illustration
+Teaches new words like clownfish, cardinal, construction worker, flamingo
+The pieces are good quality

Cons:
-The pictures with larger numbers have too many things that are too small for a young child to easily count
-In order for a toddler to clean these up, you'll need to find a replacement box
-The magnets aren't super strong

text_fidelity_a:
Repos JUST01 Just One, Various There are a lot of "just one word clues" games out there, from Codenames and Decrypto to games like Funglish, Crosstalk or Word Slam, and this game is yet another to add to that group. I think, however, that it's my secnd favorite of the bunch, and if you need a Codenames Killer, this might be up your alley.

In this team game, one player is attempting to guess a word that the rest of their team knows. Each team member writes down one word only, then compares to see if any matches are detected. If they are, those cards are discarded, and the guesser is left with fewer clues. Therefore, the more obtuse clues you get, the more you'll have, but it can be more difficult to deduce the word than if you're given a few obvious clues.

What I like about this game is that it manages to be a louder than usual team game with secrets. In Codenames or Crosstalk, two previous iterations of the concept, games are fun, but often it's players staring at the board in silence. In this one, you still can't say much, but it does lend itself to quicker play, and it's easier to communicate more freely once you have your clues written since your work is done, and the stress of the round is over for the clue-givers. This is a hard game, and it's definitely a word game, but lends itself to being an excellent family gathering game.
text_fidelity_b: Repos JUST01 Just One, Various

text_fidelity_a:
Cheerson CX-10 Mini 2.4G 4CH 6 Axis LED RC Quadcopter Toy Drone This is so awesome and it works! I thought that with how affordable it is, that it wouldn't even be able to get off the ground, but it flies great! I have to warn you that it's super hard to fly, though. This will frustrate pretty much everyone except for someone who's already an expert in quad copters. But, it's an awesome first copter to practice on. I felt that I built my skills a lot with this, and now I can fly my bigger copter a lot better than I did before I played around with this.

An awesome thing about this is that you can separately order every part of this copter. And, unlike many electronic devices, the sum of the parts is about the same as getting a new one. So, I guess you could also just get two, and when one breaks, then fix it with the other one. Or wait for them to both break and then Frankenstein a whole one back together. But, because these have such available and interchangeable parts, then I can't give it less than five stars.

The battery lasts for about five minutes of flying. Or, fifteen minutes if you're like me, and get it stuck a lot. And, the blades are all plastic, but they hurt if they run into a person. This is also really easy to get stuck on top of a roof or in a tree, so I recommend flying it in a pretty open field. They do pretty good at crash landings, too, as long as they land on grass, which was most of my landings.

It is packaged with a bunch of replacement blades, too, so you don't have to worry about breaking a few of them. They're easy to replace, too.

This listing has both the CX-10 and CX10A. The only difference is that if you depress the left stick three times on the 10A, then you go into headless mode, which is better for beginners. If you want more control, though, then you should get the CX-10. Or, you should get both, since their parts are all interchangeable.
text_fidelity_b: Cheerson CX-10 Mini 2.4G 4CH 6 Axis LED RC Quadcopter Toy Drone

As I did this at least a goodly number of the stickers stuck to the graphic and they were really on there to the point that it was really a delicate matter to pry them all off and place them back into their little punch-holes where they belong.  I bought this as a gift and its a mess that took me over an hour to fix. some sheets were almost all face down on the cardboard graphic page, ripped away from where theyre supposed to be. Two tore in spite of being careful as they are thin and were really mashed.  a simple piece of tissue would solve this.  very nice book and idea.  just packaged badly
